visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a night shot of the Tsim Sha Tsui Clock Tower, a historic red-brick structure with white clock faces illuminated against a dark sky. The camera pans down to show the base of the tower and the paved plaza area. (2) A young man in a white T-shirt and glasses walks out from a brightly lit MTR station entrance (Mong Kok Station) with red interior walls. He looks around briefly before stepping onto the street. (3) The scene shifts to night-time city streets in Hong Kong, filled with neon signs, double-decker buses, and red taxis. The man is shown walking through these crowded areas, sometimes wearing a white baseball cap, looking contemplative. (4) He is then seen leaning on a white railing overlooking a harbor at night. The background features the brilliantly lit Hong Kong Island skyline, including a Ferris wheel and numerous skyscrapers reflecting on the water. (5) Transition to a daytime scene at a colorful outdoor basketball court surrounded by rainbow-hued apartment blocks. The man stands on the court, singing and gesturing with his hands toward the camera while wearing sunglasses. (6) A montage follows, cutting between his reflective moments at the harbor, his walks through the neon-lit city, and his performance at the colorful housing estate. (7) The final shots include a wide view of the harbor skyline and an airplane on a darkened runway with hangars in the background.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: This is a music video for a Cantonese pop ballad. The core intent is to convey a sense of urban nostalgia and personal sentiment through a journey across Hong Kong's iconic night and day landscapes. By blending cinematic shots of bustling neon streets and the harbor skyline with a focused performance at the colorful Choi Hung Estate, the video aligns its visual melancholy with the song's themes of life's different paths and parting well-wishes.
